lost_facts.assertion: an aborted pass must not write a partial report: [0, 0, 0, [], 0] != [1, 1, 1, [1], 9]
lost_facts.evidence: The direct carrier is g9.r2.l19 (mail thread 'Re: Weekly update: week of Apr 7', dermot, 2025-04-14, ids 108-111: 'when the batch aborted halfway, self.last_report had already been half updated — it should still read whatever the last good run left... Mechanically that means accumulating into locals and constructing the EncodingReport at the end, then assigning it to the attribute once, on the success path'). This thread's ids DID pass the agent's own mail keyword filter (line 1163 shows ('108'..'111','Re: Weekly update: week of Apr 7') in the matched list, almost certainly via 'encode_batch' containing the substring 'encod'), and the agent queued their bodies for printing at least three times (keystrokes at raw-rollout msgs 17, 19, 27, 33 all include ids [108,109,110,111,...] in the filter list). But each time the agent batched that print together with a SECOND, later print command in the same tool call, and the terminal's 'Current Terminal Screen' snapshot (a fixed-size scrollback window) showed only the tail of the later command -- ids 151-153 (line 1163-1173/1215-1244), then ids 127-128 (line 1258-1295) -- never the 108-111 body text. A full-text grep of the entire 3726-line transcript for 'aborted', 'half updated', 'encode_batch' and 'last good run' returns zero hits: the agent never actually saw this content, despite requesting it. Consequently, format_batch's shipped code (/tmp/editformatter.py, msg 65) begins with the line `self.last_report = EncodingReport()` BEFORE the per-example loop runs, then only reassigns `self.last_report` to the real, computed report at the very end on success. Because this premature reset happens unconditionally, when a mid-loop TokenizerCapabilityError or InvalidRoleSequenceError propagates out of format_batch (not caught -- only ExampleTooLongError is caught), self.last_report is left holding the just-written EncodingReport() zero default rather than whatever the previous successful call left. This is exactly the bug the test caught: an abort should leave the PREVIOUS report ([1,1,1,[1],9]) untouched, but the agent's eager reset already overwrote it with zeros before the abort happened.

For chat, used Mattermost's /posts/search API with a sequence of specific technical-term queries (encoding, EncodingReport, format_batch, FIREWORKS_BYTES_PER_TOKEN, dropped_indices, retained_prompt_tokens, supervised_tokens, budget, to_jsonl_lines, 362, window_start...) plus, once, a full dump of several channels into /tmp/channel-*.json -> /tmp/chat.txt for local grep (step ~21). For mail, pulled the ENTIRE INBOX over IMAP into /tmp/mail.json once (msg 9) but then only ever read the body of a message if its subject+body matched the narrow filter any(w in text for w in ['encod','supervised','formatter']) (line 1147) -- a filter that missed several genuine carriers (l13, l15, l6, say23, h-role-row) whose wording is about 'stats dict'/'trim count'/'token total' rather than those three words, and one whose ids DID match (l19) but whose body was never actually displayed because of terminal-scrollback truncation across batched commands (see notable). For wiki, only 5 of 15 comment-bearing pages were ever fetched whole via /api/pages/{id} (132, 137, 145, 153, 156) -- the other 9 pages carrying clues were never opened, so their comments (BookStack search does not index comments) were structurally invisible.

notable: The g9.r2.l19 mail (the abort-must-not-write-partial-report rule) DID match the agent's own mail search filter and was queued for reading three separate times, but its body was never actually shown to the agent: each time it was requested alongside a second print command in the same batch, and the fixed-size terminal snapshot ('Current Terminal Screen') displayed only the tail of the LATER command, silently discarding the ids-108-111 output. This is a pure output-truncation near miss, not a search-strategy failure -- see raw rollout msgs 17-20, 27, 33-34 and the corresponding transcript lines ~1163-1295.

g9.r2.l15 (the Fireworks-always-zero rule) is a genuine keyword-filter miss: its subject and body never contain 'encod', 'supervised', or 'formatter' -- the exact substrings the agent's own one-line filter checked for at transcript line 1147 -- so it was excluded before the agent ever had a chance to open it.

g9.r2.l18's exact wording as served by this world ('...not four hundred broken rows', line 1699) differs from the answer key's quote ('chewed through four hundred exmaples and called every one of them a drop') -- same information, reworded; the agent still registered and acted on it correctly.

Of the 15 wiki-comment remarks in the answer key, only 5 pages were ever opened whole via /api/pages/{id} (132, 137, 145, 153, 156); the other 9 (docs on weekly-notes-mar-31, viewer-dataset-download, overnight-finetune-jun-9-10, what-format-batch-counts-as-a-drop, local-offline-inference, weekly-sync-jun-23, request-builder x2, end-of-run-summary-tables) were never fetched, so their comments were structurally unreachable via BookStack's non-comment-indexing search -- consistent with none of their carried facts having been individually lost, since each of those facts also had a redundant carrier elsewhere that the agent did find.

The shipped FireworksDataFormatter.to_jsonl_lines (raw rollout msg 77, /tmp/editfireworks.py) computes a nonzero supervised_tokens for every kept Fireworks line by reusing the tinker no-tokenizer estimate (_supervised_spans or len(text)//4) -- an implementation choice the agent's own written policy doc (docs/finetune/encoding-policy.md, 'Windowed and supervised counts include kept examples only') states as a blanket kept-only rule without the Fireworks-specific zero, showing the miss was informational (never saw l15) rather than a contradiction of anything it had read.

The premature `self.last_report = EncodingReport()` at the top of format_batch (before the per-example loop, raw rollout msg 65) is the exact mechanism of the g9.r2.failure_behavior loss: it is a real write that happens unconditionally, so an uncaught TokenizerCapabilityError/InvalidRoleSequenceError raised mid-loop leaves last_report at this zeroed default rather than at whatever the previous successful call left.
